I have what I need. Here's the plan.

---

# `intropy deploy init` — a Go-side GitOps tree generator

## Verdict up front

Generate from Go. The decision hinges on one fact: **the file set itself is the conditional part**, and `internal/template` cannot omit a file. Today an author writes `{{- if not .empty -}}…{{ end -}}` so the file exists but renders to a single newline (`internal/template/render.go` always writes a target for every walked entry). A GitOps repo cannot absorb that: an empty `dapr/pubsub.yaml` referenced from `kustomization.yaml`'s `resources:` makes `kustomize build` fail, and an empty file committed into `domains/…` is worse than no file. Add that `spec.parameters` is scalar-only (`fieldFromSchema` in `internal/template/manifest.go` recognises `string|boolean|integer|number`) with no `range` in any skeleton, and "one Dapr Component per connector, one per pubsub" is simply not expressible.

But I am *not* recommending `yaml.Marshal` for the bodies. The output is a human-owned, diff-reviewed GitOps tree that needs comments above every placeholder. So: **Go owns the model, the file set, the values and the write policy; embedded `text/template` files own the bodies**, behind a `Source` interface whose second implementation is a directory — which is exactly the seam intropy-templates can plug into later without redesigning anything. Details and the honest losses in §4 and §8.

---

## 1. Command surface

### `cmd/intropy/deploy_init.go`

```
intropy deploy init [component...] --domain <domain>
```

Zero positional args = onboard every component in the topology. Positional args filter to named components (useful on a re-run after adding one block). The subcommand name steals `init` from the component-argument space, same caveat `deploy.go`'s Long text already documents for `diff/promote/status/sync`.

**Flags**

| flag | why |
|---|---|
| `--domain` (required) | The topology has **no** notion of a GitOps domain. `Coordinate.Domain` has to come from somewhere; a flag is the honest answer for the first cut. Completion from a new `gitops.ListDomains(root)` over the cached checkout. |
| `--system` | Defaults to `topology.System`. Override for a repo whose GitOps system name differs from the .NET system name. |
| `--topology <path\|->` | Read a `topology.intropy.io/v1` record instead of running the host. **This is the primary test seam and the primary CI seam**, not an afterthought. |
| `--host <dir>` | Which system host to ask when `--topology` is absent. Defaults to discovery via `template.ListScaffolds(".")` filtered to `RoleSystemHost`, exactly as `internal/dashboard/topology.go` does. |
| `--env <name>` (repeatable) | Defaults to every environment in `deploy.yaml`, emitted in `DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()` order so the printed tree reads dev→staging→prod. |
| `--platform {beebyte\|azure}` | **Only** to seed `deploy.yaml` when it declares none; refused when it declares a different one. See §2 — this is not really a flag-shaped decision. |
| `--plan` | Render the whole tree in memory, print the file list + bodies of new files + the placeholder checklist, write nothing. Free, because the emitters never touch the filesystem. |
| `--update` / `--force` / `--adopt` | See §6. |
| `--check` | Scan the existing tree for unreplaced placeholders; generate nothing. Nonzero exit if any remain. |
| `--branch <name>` | Override the default `deploy-init/<domain>-<system>`. |
| `--no-push` | Commit the branch locally, don't push. |
| `--out <dir>` | Write the tree into a plain directory instead of the GitOps checkout, for someone who'd rather work in their own clone. Skips all git entirely. |
| `--domain/--system/--gitops-repo/--argocd-server/-o` | Standard, mirroring `deploy_sync.go`. |

### Composition with `openSession`

```go
// internal/deploy/init.go
func Init(ctx context.Context, opts InitOptions) error {
    opts.applyDefaults()
    s, err := openSession(ctx, opts.session(), "git", "kustomize")
    ...
}
```

`openSession` needs no change. `kustomize` is required because init **authors kustomizations through the binary** (§3) and because it `kustomize build`s every new overlay as an acceptance check before committing. `dotnet` is required only on the host-graph path — require it lazily, after `--topology` is ruled out, not in the `openSession` binaries list (otherwise `--topology -` in CI demands a .NET SDK for nothing).

### Commit, push, and the `ResetHard` hazard — the decisive constraint

`gitops.Repository.refresh()` does `ResetHard(origin/<branch>)` + `Clean`. **An uncommitted generated tree in the cached checkout is destroyed by the next `intropy deploy` anyone runs.** So "leave a reviewable tree in the cache" is not an option.

Nor is "commit + push to main via `Publish`". Two reasons, and the second is fatal:
1. `Publish` stages exactly `plan.RelKustomizationPath(repo.Root)` — one file. Init writes a tree.
2. `Coordinate.AppName` documents the ApplicationSet: `name: '{{index .path.segments 1}}-…-{{.cluster}}'`, generated **per overlay directory**. The instant an overlay directory lands on main, ArgoCD creates an Application for it and tries to sync a workload whose image is unpinned and whose Dapr components contain `REPLACE_ME`. Pushing a freshly generated tree to main is a self-inflicted incident.

**So: a branch, and a PR.**

```go
// internal/git/client.go — three small additions
func (g Client) CheckoutNewBranch(ctx context.Context, name, startPoint string) error // checkout -b
func (g Client) CheckoutBranch(ctx context.Context, name string) error                // checkout
func (g Client) DeleteBranch(ctx context.Context, name string) error                  // branch -D
```

No new push method needed — `Client.Push(ctx, remote, refspec)` already takes a raw refspec, so `Push(ctx, gitops.RemoteName, "HEAD:refs/heads/"+branch)` works.

Sequence, and note the last two steps:

```
CheckoutNewBranch(branch, "origin/"+repo.Branch)
write tree; kustomize-author kustomizations; kustomize build every new overlay
Add(<each generated path>)            // explicit paths, never `add -A` — same rule Publish states
Commit(subject, trailers)
Push(origin, "HEAD:refs/heads/"+branch)
CheckoutBranch(repo.Branch)           // ← restore the shared cache
DeleteBranch(branch)                  // ← leave no debris for the next run
```

Without the last two, `refresh()` on the next run resets the *side branch* to `origin/main` and leaves HEAD on it — not catastrophic (deploy's refspec is the explicit `HEAD:main`) but confusing debris in a shared cache. Restore it.

**No rebase-retry loop.** `Publish`'s `maxPushAttempts` machinery exists because two deploys edit the same line of the same file. A fresh branch cannot be rejected by a concurrent deploy. If the *remote branch already exists*, that's a real signal: refuse, name it, suggest `--branch`. Don't force-push into someone's open PR.

Commit subject and trailers, consistent with `internal/deploy/publish.go`'s format (which `deploy history` parses, so new keys must be additive):

```
deploy(init): onboard order-flow (3 components, 3 environments)

Deploy-Domain: orders
Deploy-System: order-flow
Deploy-Init-Components: order-extractor, order-loader, order-reconciler
Deploy-Init-Placeholders: 7
Deploy-By: …
Deploy-Cli: …
```

Body carries the placeholder checklist verbatim, so the PR description *is* the developer's to-do list. That directly serves the stated goal.

### Output and exit codes

`--plan` and `-o json` mirror the existing pattern: `report()` in `internal/deploy/service.go` writes plain to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, and JSON is the sole stdout content in JSON mode. New result type in `internal/deploy/result.go`:

```go
type InitResult struct {
    Domain, System, Platform string           `json:"…"`
    Branch     string   `json:"branch,omitempty"`
    Revision   string   `json:"revision,omitempty"`
    Applied    bool     `json:"applied"`
    Units      []InitUnit     `json:"units"`
    Files      []InitFile     `json:"files"`        // path + action: create|unchanged|modified|obsolete
    Placeholders []InitPlaceholder `json:"placeholders,omitempty"`
}
```

Exit codes: unchanged table from `cmd/intropy/main.go`. `2` for missing `--domain`, unknown `--platform`, `--force` with `--plan`; `127` for missing `git`/`kustomize`/`dotnet` (inherited via `command.ErrNotInstalled`); `1` when `--check` finds placeholders. I'd resist adding a code `3`; a distinct code is nice for CI but the message and the JSON already carry the detail, and the code table is documented in three places.

**Completions.** `--env` → existing `completeDeployEnvironments`. `--domain` → new `completeDeployDomains` over `gitops.CachedRoot`. `--topology` → `MarkFlagFilename("json")`. Positional args: **no completion**, `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`. `completeDeployComponents` lists components that are *already onboarded* — exactly the ones init doesn't apply to — and the correct source (the topology) requires `dotnet build`, which violates the "instant and offline" rule every completion in `deploy.go` obeys.

---

## 2. The deployment model

New package **`internal/manifests`**. It mirrors `internal/system` exactly — `model.go` (the IR), `assemble.go` (topology → IR), `emit.go` (IR → bytes) — which is the closest prior art in the repo for "generate files from a declarative model" and which keeps `internal/deploy` (already 8 files, ~120 KB) as pure orchestration.

### `internal/manifests/model.go`

```go
// Plan is the complete desired file set for one system, plus the values that
// produced it. Everything after Assemble reads this and never the topology.
type Plan struct {
	Domain   string
	System   string
	Registry string            // deploy.yaml registry
	Units    []Unit            // one per topology component, sorted by coordinate
	Shared   Shared            // system-scoped Dapr resources (see §8, open question 1)
	Envs     []Environment     // in DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()
}

// Environment is one target: its name, the platform it runs on, and the
// namespace its overlays set. Platform is per-environment because a customer
// mid-migration runs dev on beebyte and prod on Azure, and the Dapr component
// type is the thing that differs.
type Environment struct {
	Name      string
	Platform  string // gitops.PlatformBeebyte | gitops.PlatformAzure
	Namespace string
	Sync      string // carried for the report only; init enforces nothing
}

// Unit is one deployable component: exactly one GitOps coordinate, one image,
// one workload shape. The unit is the atom because the ApplicationSet
// generates one Application per overlay directory — nothing smaller can be
// deployed or promoted independently.
type Unit struct {
	Coordinate gitops.Coordinate // Domain / System / topology Component.Name
	Kind       string            // topology Component.Kind, verbatim
	AppID      string            // Dapr app-id; == Coordinate.Component
	Workload   Workload
	Image      string            // <registry>/integrations/<component>, bare — no tag, no digest

	// AppPort is the HTTP port the Dapr sidecar delivers to. Zero for a
	// CronJob, which has no server to deliver to.
	AppPort int

	// Schedule is the CronJob cron. Always a placeholder: the topology carries
	// no cron, even though the generated SystemClass.cs already calls
	// .WithSchedule("* * * * *").
	Schedule string

	Subscribes []TopicRef // (pubsub, topic) pairs, from Component.Subscribes
	Publishes  []TopicRef // from Component.Publishes
	Bindings   []Binding  // one per Component.Connectors entry
	Secrets    []SecretKey
}

type Workload string

const (
	// WorkloadCronJob is a run-to-completion block. The extractor template's
	// own description says scheduling is external — "a Kubernetes CronJob in
	// production".
	WorkloadCronJob Workload = "CronJob"

	// WorkloadDeployment is a long-running block: the loader subscribes over
	// HTTP delivery, so it must be up to receive.
	WorkloadDeployment Workload = "Deployment"
)

// Binding is one connector-backed Dapr Component. Name is
// "binding.<connector>" — the exact string the scaffolded Constants.cs
// resolves at runtime (InboundBindingName), so a mismatch here is a runtime
// "component not found", not a compile error.
type Binding struct {
	Name           string
	Connector      string
	ExternalSystem string
	Transport      string // topology Transport.Type: http | sftp | file
	Direction      string // input | output | input,output
	Type           string // Dapr spec.type, chosen from (Transport, Platform)
	Metadata       []Field
}

// Field is one spec.metadata entry. Exactly one of Value and SecretKeyRef is
// set: a credential never becomes a literal, not even a placeholder one.
type Field struct {
	Name         string
	Value        string
	SecretKeyRef *SecretKey
	Doc          string // the comment emitted above it
}

type SecretKey struct {
	Secret string // Kubernetes Secret name
	Key    string
	Doc    string
}

// Shared are the system-scoped Dapr resources: one pubsub per distinct
// Topic.PubSub the topology names, plus the platform services every block
// expects (idempotency, business-incident).
type Shared struct {
	PubSubs       []PubSub
	StateStores   []StateStore
	HTTPEndpoints []HTTPEndpoint
}

type PubSub struct {
	Name     string   // topology PubSub name — "pubsub" by convention
	Type     string   // pubsub.azure.servicebus.topics | pubsub.rabbitmq
	Topics   []string // for scoping / declarative topic creation
	Metadata []Field
}
```

`FromTopology` is a pure function with no IO, which is what makes step 2 of the work breakdown a fast table-driven test:

```go
// internal/manifests/assemble.go
type Options struct {
	Domain, System string
	Registry       string
	Envs           []Environment
	Only           []string                 // positional filter; empty = all
	Warnf          func(string, ...any)
}

func FromTopology(t *topology.Topology, opts Options) (*Plan, error)
```

Mapping rules, all in one place:

| topology | model |
|---|---|
| `Component.Kind == "extractor"` | `WorkloadCronJob`, `AppPort: 0`, `Schedule: Placeholder("cron", name)` |
| `Component.Kind ∈ {loader, transactionalIntegration, aggregator}` | `WorkloadDeployment`, `AppPort: 8080` |
| unknown `Kind` | **error** listing the kinds it knows — `Assemble` in `internal/system` warns-and-skips, but there skipping loses a `From/To`; here it would silently not deploy a component |
| `Component.Connectors[i]` + matching `Connectors[]` | one `Binding`, `Name: "binding."+connector` |
| `Transport.Type` × `Platform` | `Binding.Type` (§3 table) |
| distinct `Topics[].PubSub` | one `Shared.PubSub` per name, `Type` from platform |
| `Topics[].Topic` | `PubSub.Topics` entry |
| `Contracts`, `APIs`, `Provides`, `Consumes` | **ignored** — nothing in a K8s manifest depends on a message schema |

Validation `FromTopology` must do, because these are silent runtime failures otherwise: `Component.Name` is DNS-1123 kebab, and `len(Coordinate.AppName(env)) <= 63` for every env (it becomes an ArgoCD Application name derived from path segments; blowing the label budget fails at reconcile time with an opaque message).

### Where the platform lives — exact schema addition

Not a flag. The cloud is a property of the *cluster the GitOps repo feeds*, and a flag means two operators disagree and a re-run silently flips every Dapr component. `deploy.yaml`, with a per-environment override, because dev-on-beebyte / prod-on-Azure is the migration case that motivates the whole feature.

```go
// internal/gitops/config.go
const (
	PlatformBeebyte = "beebyte"
	PlatformAzure   = "azure"
)

type DeployConfig struct {
	SchemaVersion     int    `yaml:"schemaVersion"`
	Registry          string `yaml:"registry"`
	MinimumCliVersion string `yaml:"minimumCliVersion"`

	// Platform names the cloud the cluster runs on, which decides which
	// backing service a generated Dapr component targets. Optional: an absent
	// value means the repository predates `deploy init`, and init asks for
	// --platform rather than guessing. Nothing but generation reads it —
	// deploy, promote, diff, status and sync are platform-blind.
	Platform string `yaml:"platform,omitempty"`

	Argocd       ArgocdConfig                 `yaml:"argocd"`
	Environments map[string]EnvironmentConfig `yaml:"environments"`
}

type EnvironmentConfig struct {
	Sync                 string   `yaml:"sync"`
	PromotesFrom         []string `yaml:"promotesFrom"`
	RequireSourceHealthy bool     `yaml:"requireSourceHealthy"`
	Scratch              bool     `yaml:"scratch"`

	// Platform overrides the repository-level platform for this environment,
	// for a repository whose environments do not all run on the same cloud.
	Platform string `yaml:"platform,omitempty"`

	// Namespace is the Kubernetes namespace this environment's overlays set.
	// Optional; defaults to the environment name.
	Namespace string `yaml:"namespace,omitempty"`
}

// Platform returns the platform for env: the environment's own when set,
// otherwise the repository's. Empty when neither declares one.
func (c *DeployConfig) Platform(env string) string
```

`validate()` rejects an unrecognised platform value (repo-level and per-env) but does **not** require one — every existing repo has none.

**Compatibility hazard worth surfacing to the user now.** `decodeFile` sets `dec.KnownFields(true)`. Adding `platform:` to a repo's `deploy.yaml` makes **every older `intropy` binary fail to parse it** — including `deploy`, `promote` and `sync`, i.e. the whole pipeline, for anyone who hasn't upgraded. That is precisely what `minimumCliVersion` exists for. So `deploy init` should, when it writes `platform:` into `deploy.yaml`, also raise `minimumCliVersion` to the current CLI in the same commit, and say so on stdout. It is not a `SchemaVersion` bump (additive fields don't need one per the constant's own doc comment), but it *is* a fleet-upgrade event.

---

## 3. The emitters

Two tiers, split by a single criterion: **does the CLI also need to read this file back?**

### Tier 1 — files the CLI reasons about: typed Go, or the kustomize binary

**`component.yaml`** — there is already a type: `gitops.ComponentConfig`. Build it, `yaml.Marshal` it, then **round-trip it through `gitops.LoadComponentConfig`** before writing. That self-check is nearly free and catches every future drift between the emitter and the validator (`images` non-empty, bare repository names, `environments` non-empty, `schemaVersion`). Field order comes from struct order, so it's deterministic. Comments: the file is 6 lines and self-explanatory; skip them.

```go
func (u Unit) ComponentConfig(envs []string) gitops.ComponentConfig {
	return gitops.ComponentConfig{
		SchemaVersion: gitops.SchemaVersion,
		Name:          u.Coordinate.Component,
		SourcePaths:   []string{u.Coordinate.Component + "/"},
		Images:        []gitops.ImageRef{{Name: u.Image}},
		Environments:  envs,
	}
}
```

**`kustomization.yaml` (base and every overlay)** — do **not** hand-write these. `internal/kustomize/editor.go` states the rule explicitly: *"kustomize owns writes, so unmodelled fields cannot be lost."* Init should honour it, and that means three additions:

```go
// internal/kustomize/editor.go
func (k Client) Create(ctx context.Context, dir string, resources ...string) error // kustomize create --resources a,b
func (k Client) AddResource(ctx context.Context, dir, path string) error           // kustomize edit add resource
func (k Client) SetNamespace(ctx context.Context, dir, ns string) error            // kustomize edit set namespace
```

Cost, stated honestly: `kustomize create`'s exact formatting is kustomize's, so a kustomize version bump can change the bytes of a file we've hashed for idempotency (§6). I accept it, because (a) the file is five lines, (b) the alternative is the CLI owning kustomization-file semantics forever, and (c) `--update` reclassifies it as "generated by an older toolchain" rather than "you edited it", which is the correct message anyway.

**Crucially: init never writes `images:` into an overlay.** The overlay ships unpinned; `intropy deploy` pins the digest. This is the rule that killed `manifests create` ("it pinned `newTag: latest`, contradicting the digest-pinning rule") and it must be stated in the package doc so nobody re-adds it. It also means the first `deploy` after an init is the acceptance test of the whole tree.

### Tier 2 — bodies humans read: `embed.FS` + `text/template`

```
internal/manifests/
  embed.go                     //go:embed all:bodies
  bodies/
    deployment.yaml.tmpl
    cronjob.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/pubsub.azure.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/pubsub.beebyte.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/binding.sftp.azure.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/binding.sftp.beebyte.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/binding.http.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/binding.file.yaml.tmpl
    dapr/statestore.azure.yaml.tmpl
    secret.yaml.tmpl
```

`web/embed.go` is the in-repo precedent for `embed.FS`. Rendered with `text/template` + `sprig.TxtFuncMap()` — the same engine `internal/system/codegen.go` and `internal/template/render.go` already use, so there is one templating dialect in the CLI, not two.

Why text templates for bodies rather than structs + `yaml.Marshal`:

- **Comments.** `yaml.v3` can emit them, but only by hand-building a `yaml.Node` tree with `HeadComment`/`LineComment`. That is ten times the code and unreadable. Every placeholder in this tree needs a comment saying what to put there — that *is* the feature the user asked for.
- **Reviewability of the generator.** A platform engineer can read `bodies/cronjob.yaml.tmpl` and know what will be produced. Nobody can read `emitCronJob()` and predict output. This concession is deliberate: it preserves the single best property of the template-driven alternative while keeping the *decisions* in Go.
- **Blank-line grouping and key order** come free and stay stable across CLI versions as long as the file doesn't change — which is exactly the stability property the generated-record hashes depend on.

The `Source` seam — the thing that makes the intropy-templates question a follow-up rather than a fork in the road:

```go
// internal/manifests/source.go

// Source resolves a body template by its logical name, e.g.
// "cronjob.yaml" or "dapr/pubsub.azure.yaml".
type Source interface {
	Open(name string) (io.ReadCloser, error)
}

func Embedded() Source              // bodies/, compiled in
func Dir(root string) Source        // a directory of overrides
func Layered(s ...Source) Source    // first hit wins

// Render turns a Plan into the complete desired tree: repo-relative
// slash-separated path -> bytes, deterministically ordered. It touches no
// filesystem, which is what makes --plan free and the tests trivial.
type Tree map[string][]byte
func Render(p *Plan, src Source) (Tree, error)
```

`Render` producing an in-memory `Tree` rather than writing is the single most load-bearing shape decision in the whole design: `--plan`, `--check`, the idempotency classification (§6) and the tests all fall out of it.

Platform conditionality lives in one table, not scattered through templates:

| Transport / need | beebyte | azure |
|---|---|---|
| pubsub | `pubsub.rabbitmq` | `pubsub.azure.servicebus.topics` |
| statestore (idempotency) | `state.redis` | `state.azure.cosmosdb` |
| `sftp` connector | `bindings.sftp` | `bindings.sftp` |
| `http` connector | `bindings.http` | `bindings.http` |
| `file` connector | `bindings.localstorage` + PVC note | `bindings.azure.blobstorage` |

(The exact right-hand column is the user's to confirm — that's open question 6.) Note the `file` row: the local skeleton uses `bindings.localstorage` with a `rootPath`, which in a cluster means a volume that nobody has provisioned. Init should emit the binding *plus* a comment saying so, not pretend.

Emitted tree for one unit, three environments:

```
domains/orders/order-flow/order-extractor/
  component.yaml                        # gitops.ComponentConfig, round-tripped
  .intropy-generated.yaml               # §6
  base/
    kustomization.yaml                  # kustomize create --resources cronjob.yaml
    cronjob.yaml                        # embedded body; image = <registry>/integrations/…:PLACEHOLDER-free bare ref
  overlays/dev/
    kustomization.yaml                  # kustomize create; set namespace; add resources
    dapr/binding.order-extractor-source.yaml
    secret.yaml                         # stub, stringData with placeholders
  overlays/staging/  …
  overlays/prod/     …
```

Dapr components and the Secret stub go in the **overlay**, not the base, for two reasons that are the same reason: the platform can differ per environment, and connection strings always do.

---

## 4. Where `intropy-templates` still fits

The honest answer, in three layers, only the first of which ships in the first cut:

**Layer 1 (ships): embedded.** `Embedded()` is the only `Source`.

**Layer 2 (cheap follow-up, and the one I'd actually build next): overrides in the GitOps repo itself.**

```yaml
# deploy.yaml
manifests:
  overridesDir: .intropy/manifests    # relative to the GitOps repo root
```
→ `Layered(Dir(filepath.Join(repo.Root, cfg.Manifests.OverridesDir)), Embedded())`.

This beats intropy-templates on every axis for the customer-specific case: the override is versioned *with the cluster it customises*, reviewed in the same PR as the tree it produced, needs no network, needs no tag, and a platform engineer editing `.intropy/manifests/deployment.yaml.tmpl` never leaves the repo they already have open. If someone needs a `NetworkPolicy` for one customer, this is the mechanism.

**Layer 3 (only if the user still wants it): pinned intropy-templates.**

```yaml
manifests:
  template: gitops-component
  version: v1.4.0        # pinned in deploy.yaml — not "latest"
```
→ `Layered(Dir(overrides), tarball(gitops-component@v1.4.0), Embedded())`, reusing `template.NewGitHubClient` / `DownloadTemplate`. The **version must be pinned in `deploy.yaml`**, which is what makes this defensible: it restores reproducibility (the thing whose absence killed `manifests create`), and it makes the choice a repo-level decision rather than an invocation-level accident. `deploy init` has no `.intropy/scaffold.json` to read a pinned tag from — it runs against the GitOps repo, from any directory — so `deploy.yaml` is the only place a tag *can* live.

Two costs of layer 3 that are easy to underestimate:
- **No cache.** `internal/template/github.go` re-downloads the whole `intropy-templates` tarball on every render. `deploy init` already refreshes a GitOps clone; adding a second unconditional multi-megabyte fetch to the same command is a real regression in a command people will run repeatedly while iterating on placeholders.
- **Only bodies, never the file set.** Even in layer 3, `Render` decides *which* templates to open. A template that isn't opened isn't rendered — which is, incidentally, the conditional-file-omission feature, obtained for free by inverting control.

### If you'd rather extend `internal/template` instead

Two changes would be required, and I'd price them honestly:

1. **Whole-file omission.** Cleanest form is an explicit manifest section rather than a magic file:
   ```yaml
   spec:
     files:
       - path: dapr/pubsub.yaml
         when: '{{ eq .platform "azure" }}'
   ```
   `Render` grows a predicate check before `renderTemplate`. ~40 lines. But it means `Render` needs the file list *and* the values, and `Render(srcDir, destDir, values)` currently has no manifest access — its doc comment says "the manifest lives outside this tree". So the signature changes, and `int create` / `sys create` / `template.Create` all move with it.

2. **List- and object-typed parameters.** This is the expensive one. `FieldSpec.Type` is scalar-only; `coerce`, `applySetValues`, `ParseSets` (`key=value` strings), `AutoPrompter` and `missingRequired`/`isEmpty` all assume scalars. Worse: `spec.parameters` is documented in `intropy-templates/CLAUDE.md` as *"the same schema [that] validates CLI inputs and drives the Backstage form"*. Array-of-object parameters are exactly what a JSON-Schema-driven form renders worst. So the cost isn't the Go code — it's that you'd be degrading the template format's *other* consumer to serve a generator that has a first-class Go model available to it anyway.

That asymmetry is the core of my recommendation: the template format is optimised for *a human filling in a form*, and `deploy init` is optimised for *a machine reading a graph*. Bodies are the overlap; parameters are not.

---

## 5. Placeholders

### The marker

```go
// internal/manifests/placeholder.go

// Marker is the fixed token every unfilled value carries. All-caps, no "$",
// no braces, no colon: it must survive `kustomize build` untouched (kustomize
// treats $(…) as a replacement reference), stay a plain YAML scalar without
// quoting, and be greppable with one fixed string.
const Marker = "REPLACE_ME"

// Placeholder renders REPLACE_ME__<KIND>__<HINT>, e.g.
// REPLACE_ME__CONNECTION_STRING__SERVICEBUS or REPLACE_ME__CRON__ORDER_EXTRACTOR.
func Placeholder(kind, hint string) string

type Found struct {
	File string // repo-relative, slash-separated
	Line int
	Kind string // connection-string | cron | url | host | secret-key | account
	Hint string
	Text string // the full marker as it appears
}

// Scan walks a rendered tree (or an on-disk fs.FS) and reports every marker.
func Scan(t Tree) []Found
func ScanFS(fsys fs.FS) ([]Found, error)
```

The `__KIND__HINT` shape earns its keep twice: it makes the checklist self-describing without a lookup table, and it makes a stray placeholder **fail loudly rather than partially**. `schedule: REPLACE_ME__CRON__ORDER_EXTRACTOR` is rejected by the API server, so the CronJob is never created. A placeholder that happened to be a valid-but-wrong value would be far more dangerous.

Credentials never become placeholder literals. They become a `secretKeyRef` into a stub Secret:

```yaml
# overlays/prod/secret.yaml — created by `intropy deploy init`.
# Replace every REPLACE_ME__* below with the real value, then move this file
# out of git: sealed-secrets, SOPS or External Secrets, per your platform.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: order-extractor-secrets
type: Opaque
stringData:
  # Azure Service Bus connection string with Send rights on topic "orders".
  # Portal: Service Bus namespace -> Shared access policies.
  servicebus-connection-string: REPLACE_ME__CONNECTION_STRING__SERVICEBUS
```

That `# then move this file out of git` line matters: init must not normalise committing plaintext secrets, so the stub says what to do instead and the checklist repeats it.

### Reporting

Plain output, grouped by file, after the file-action list:

```
7 placeholders to fill in before this can deploy:

  overlays/prod/secret.yaml
    :12  connection-string  servicebus   Azure Service Bus connection string (Send on "orders")
    :16  host               acme-sftp    Hostname of the ACME SFTP server
  base/cronjob.yaml
    :9   cron               order-extractor   How often the extractor sweeps its source

  intropy deploy init --check order-extractor    # re-run this when you're done
```

JSON carries `placeholders[]`. The commit body carries the same list, so the PR is the checklist.

### Detection before it reaches a cluster — two gates

**Gate 1, `--check`.** Scans the on-disk tree (`ScanFS` over the component dir), generates nothing, exits 1 with the list. The CI gate.

**Gate 2, and this is the important one: `intropy deploy` refuses.** `BuildPlan` in `internal/deploy/plan.go` already renders the overlay, normalises it, and runs exactly one guard of this shape — `assertPinsRendered(afterNorm, opts.Pins)` — inside a revert-protected block. Add a sibling immediately after it:

```go
// internal/deploy/plan.go, right after assertPinsRendered
if err := assertNoPlaceholders(afterNorm); err != nil {
	return nil, withRevert(err, revert)
}
```

```go
// assertNoPlaceholders refuses to deploy a render that still carries an
// unfilled placeholder from `deploy init`. The render, not the files: a
// placeholder in a file kustomize does not include cannot reach the cluster,
// and failing on it would block a deploy for a resource nobody applies.
func assertNoPlaceholders(rendered []byte) error
```

Roughly 15 lines, inherits revert-on-failure for free, and it is the guard that makes the whole placeholder story safe. Reporting the *resource identities* rather than file paths is the right call here — the render has no file paths — and `kustomize.Identities` already exists for exactly that.

Checking the **render** rather than the files is deliberate and worth the comment: a `secret.yaml` a developer chose not to include in `kustomization.yaml` (because they use External Secrets instead) must not block deploys forever.

---

## 6. Idempotency and re-runs

The hardest part, so here are the rules in priority order, with the reasoning that makes each one non-negotiable.

**Rule 1 — never modify a file that exists.** Default is create-only. A file on disk is the human's. This is the only rule a reviewer can verify at a glance, and it makes re-running unconditionally safe, which is what makes the command usable at all.

**Rule 2 — report the delta, don't apply it.** `Render` gives the complete desired `Tree`; classify each path against disk:

```go
// internal/manifests/apply.go
type Action string
const (
	ActionCreate    Action = "create"    // missing; init writes it
	ActionUnchanged Action = "unchanged" // exists, bytes match the record's hash
	ActionModified  Action = "modified"  // exists, differs — a human edited it, or the CLI changed
	ActionObsolete  Action = "obsolete"  // recorded, but this Plan no longer produces it
	ActionForeign   Action = "foreign"   // exists, no record — hand-onboarded before init
)

type FileAction struct {
	Path   string
	Action Action
	Reason string   // phrased, printed verbatim
}

func Classify(t Tree, root string, rec *gitops.GeneratedRecord) ([]FileAction, error)
func Apply(t Tree, root string, actions []FileAction, mode Mode) ([]string, error)
```

`ActionObsolete` is **reported, never deleted**. A connector removed from the topology may still be needed by the image currently running in prod; deleting its Dapr Component while the old pods are alive is an outage. The line says: *"`overlays/prod/dapr/binding.legacy-sftp.yaml` is no longer in the topology — remove it once prod runs an image that doesn't use it."*

**Rule 3 — make "still mine" checkable without storing bytes.** A per-component record beside `component.yaml`:

```
domains/<d>/<s>/<c>/.intropy-generated.yaml
```
```yaml
schemaVersion: 1
cli: v0.9.0
generatedAt: 2026-07-28T09:12:03Z
platform: azure
topologyFingerprint: sha256:3f2a…      # over this unit's slice of the topology
files:
  base/kustomization.yaml: sha256:…
  base/cronjob.yaml: sha256:…
  overlays/prod/dapr/binding.order-extractor-source.yaml: sha256:…
```

```go
// internal/gitops/generated.go
const GeneratedFileName = ".intropy-generated.yaml"

type GeneratedRecord struct {
	SchemaVersion       int               `yaml:"schemaVersion"`
	Cli                 string            `yaml:"cli"`
	GeneratedAt         time.Time         `yaml:"generatedAt"`
	Platform            string            `yaml:"platform,omitempty"`
	TopologyFingerprint string            `yaml:"topologyFingerprint,omitempty"`
	Files               map[string]string `yaml:"files"`
}

func LoadGenerated(dir string) (*GeneratedRecord, error)   // fs.ErrNotExist is not an error to callers
func WriteGenerated(dir string, r GeneratedRecord) error
```

Same instincts as `.intropy/scaffold.json` (schemaVersion, additive fields, `KnownFields(true)` via `decodeFile`). It buys three things at once: exact `unchanged`/`modified` classification with no network and no template fetch; `obsolete` detection; and — via `cli:` — the answer to "stability across CLI versions". When the emitters change, files nobody touched hash-mismatch, and the record lets init say *"generated by v0.8.0; this CLI would write it differently"* instead of the false and infuriating *"you edited this"*.

Keep it a separate file rather than a `generated:` block in `component.yaml`: folding it in would make init rewrite `component.yaml` on every run — the one file that also carries hand-maintained `sourcePaths` and `images`, and therefore the one file Rule 1 protects hardest.

**Rule 4 — `--force` is graduated, and `--update` is the useful one.**

| mode | behaviour |
|---|---|
| (default) | create missing only. Report `modified`, `obsolete`, `foreign`. |
| `--update` | additionally rewrite files whose **recorded hash still matches** — i.e. provably not human-edited. This is "the CLI improved, regenerate what's still mine", and it's the mode people will actually use. `modified` files are still untouched. |
| `--force` | rewrite everything the Plan produces, including human edits. Prints every clobbered path. Safe only because the tree is committed on a branch, so the edits are recoverable from git. |
| `--adopt` | write the record for files that already match what init *would* generate, converting a hand-built tree into a managed one. The adoption path, and it costs almost nothing. |

**Explicitly rejected: three-way merge.** There is no common ancestor unless the record stores original *bytes* rather than hashes (bloating a file in a repo humans browse); Kubernetes YAML merges badly at the text level; and a bad merge in a GitOps repo is a production incident, not a rebase conflict. `--update`-when-hash-matches captures most of the value at a fraction of the risk. This is the strongest opinion in the plan and I'd defend it hard.

**Topology drift, case by case:**

- **new component** → a whole new coordinate, pure create, zero conflict. The common case, and it must be frictionless (`intropy deploy init --domain orders` after `intropy int create`).
- **new topic** → possibly nothing at all on the manifest side. The scaffolded loader subscribes programmatically over HTTP delivery (`/dapr/subscribe`), not via a declarative `Subscription` manifest — so a new topic changes the *code*, not the tree. It may add a `PubSub.Topics` entry for Azure scoping. Worth a comment so nobody looks for the missing file.
- **removed connector** → `ActionObsolete`, report only.
- **renamed component** → looks like one new coordinate plus one obsolete coordinate. init must not be clever. Report both and let the human decide.
- **platform flipped for one environment** → every Dapr Component in that overlay becomes `modified` (they're generated, so `--update` handles it cleanly) — but the *Secret keys change too*, so the report must call out that the new components reference secret keys the existing Secret doesn't have. Concretely: run `Scan` on the newly rendered tree and diff the `secretKeyRef` set against the existing Secret's `stringData` keys. Cheap, and it's the difference between "regenerated" and "regenerated and working".
- **partially hand-onboarded** (the realistic first encounter): `component.yaml` and `base/` exist, one overlay exists, no record. Everything existing is `foreign`, missing overlays are `create`. init proceeds, creates what's missing, and suggests `--adopt`.

---

## 7. Sequencing (TDD-shaped)

Every step is testable with the conventions in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: Go string-constant fixtures, `t.TempDir()`, real git via `internal/gittest`, GitOps fixtures via `gitopstest.NewRepo`, real `kustomize` behind a `requireKustomize(t)` skip (the pattern at `internal/deploy/plan_test.go:16`), `command.Runner` injected.

**Step 0 — decisions before code.** Open questions 1, 2 and 6 in §8. Question 6 in particular can shrink steps 2–3 by half.

**Step 1 — `internal/gitops`: platform + namespace.**
Tests: `platform: azure` parses; unknown value rejected with the valid list; per-env override beats repo-level; absent → `""`; `Namespace(env)` defaults to the env name; `ListDomains` sorted and deduped. Plus one test asserting that an *older-shaped* deploy.yaml (no `platform`) still parses — the compatibility direction that matters.

**Step 2 — `internal/manifests/model.go` + `assemble.go`.** Pure, no IO.
Tests: a string-constant topology JSON → `topology.Decode` → `FromTopology` → asserted `Plan`. Cases: extractor→CronJob with a cron placeholder; loader→Deployment with `AppPort`; `transactionalIntegration`→Deployment with two bindings; unknown kind→error naming known kinds; azure vs beebyte pubsub type; two components on one pubsub → one `Shared.PubSub`; `Only` filter; non-kebab component name rejected; `AppName` over 63 chars rejected.

**Step 3 — `internal/manifests/embed.go`, `source.go`, `emit.go`.**
Tests: `Render` output compared against full expected bodies as string constants (no golden files — that's the house rule and it's the right one here, because a golden file would let a body change slip through review); the same `Plan` renders byte-identical twice; `Layered(Dir(tmp), Embedded())` picks the override; a body referencing a missing value fails loudly (`missingkey=error`).

**Step 4 — `placeholder.go`.** `Placeholder` formatting, `Scan` over a `Tree`, `ScanFS`, line numbers correct, the checklist rendering.

**Step 5 — `internal/gitops/generated.go` + `internal/manifests/apply.go`.**
Tests over `t.TempDir()`: all five `Action` values; `--update` rewrites `unchanged` and spares `modified`; `--adopt` writes a record for byte-matching foreign files; `obsolete` is never deleted; a record from a newer `schemaVersion` is refused.

**Step 6 — `internal/kustomize` + `internal/git` additions.** Small, mechanical, each with one test through `command.Runner` plus one real-binary test behind the skip.

**Step 7 — `internal/deploy/init.go`.** Orchestration: `openSession`, topology acquisition, `FromTopology`, `Render`, `Classify`, `--plan` report, `Apply`, kustomize-author the kustomizations, **`kustomize build` every new overlay as an acceptance check before committing**, branch/commit/push, restore the cache.
Tests: `gitopstest.NewRepo` for the origin, `--topology -` fed a string constant so no `dotnet`; assert the committed tree, that the cache is back on the default branch with the temp branch gone, that `--plan` writes nothing and leaves the checkout clean, that a pre-existing remote branch is refused, and that a component already fully onboarded is a no-op.

**Step 8 — topology acquisition, shared with the dashboard.** Lift `runGraphVerb` out of `internal/dashboard/topology.go` into `internal/topology/hostgraph.go`:

```go
func RunGraph(ctx context.Context, r command.Runner, hostDir string) (*Topology, error)
func FindHosts(root string) []string   // template.ListScaffolds filtered to RoleSystemHost
```
Two notes: it currently uses `exec.CommandContext` directly, so threading `command.Runner` is a small but real improvement (it makes the dotnet path fakeable, which is the only way `deploy init`'s default path gets a test); and the dashboard's `graphTimeout` of 5 minutes plus `tail()` should move with it unchanged.

**Step 9 — `cmd/intropy/deploy_init.go`.** Flags, completions, usage errors, `--check`. cmd-level test through the real `rootCmd`, as `deploy_test.go` does.

**Step 10 — the deploy gate.** `assertNoPlaceholders` in `internal/deploy/plan.go`. Regression test: an overlay containing `REPLACE_ME` refuses to deploy, names the offending resource, and the overlay is reverted.

**Follow-ups, in order of value:** system-scoped Dapr resources (question 1); the `Dir` override layer; `Scaffold.Gitops{Domain,System,Component}` written back into the component repo's `.intropy/scaffold.json` (additive, no bump — and it's what would let `deploy` stop guessing via `FindComponent`); a placeholder count column in `deploy status`; pinned intropy-templates as a third `Source`.

**Cross-repo prereqs:**
- **intropy-templates: none for the first cut.** That is a feature, not an omission.
- **intropy-topology / the .NET host:** the single highest-value addition is `Component.Schedule`. The generated `SystemClass.cs` already emits `.WithSchedule("* * * * *")` (`internal/system/codegen.go`, `defaultExtractorSchedule`), so the declaration *has* the cron and the record just doesn't carry it. Second: an app port for HTTP-delivery blocks. Connector addresses should stay out — those are per-environment and belong in placeholders by design.
- **The GitOps repo / ApplicationSet:** only if system-scoped resources land outside `domains/`.

---

## 8. Risks and open questions

### Where the template-driven alternative wins

I'd rather state these plainly than pretend the choice is free.

1. **Customer-specific manifests without a CLI release.** A customer needs a `PodDisruptionBudget`, a `NetworkPolicy`, a specific `securityContext`, an Istio `VirtualService`. With embedded bodies that's a CLI PR, a release, and a fleet upgrade. With a template library it's a tag. **This is the strongest argument against my recommendation**, and it's the entire reason the `Source` interface exists from day one even though only `Embedded()` is implemented — without that seam, this objection becomes a rewrite instead of a follow-up.
2. **Non-Go authors.** The people who know the cluster are platform engineers. They will happily edit `skeleton/base/deployment.yaml.tmpl`. They will not send a Go PR. Embedded `text/template` files preserve most of this (they're still YAML with `{{ }}`), which is precisely why I refused `yaml.Marshal` for bodies — but a contribution still requires a CLI build and release.
3. **Predictability of the generator.** Reading a skeleton tells you the output. Reading `Render` + a body template + a platform table is three files. This is a genuine ergonomic loss and the reason the platform matrix must stay a single table.
4. **The platform matrix grows.** azure + beebyte today. Add AWS and GCP and the Go conditionals become a switch nest, while a template library gets one directory per platform for free.
5. **Backstage.** `intropy-templates` already feeds the Backstage scaffolder form. A `gitops-component` template there could be surfaced in Backstage; embedded bodies can never be.
6. **One story instead of two.** "Where do skeletons live?" currently has one answer. Two answers is a real cognitive cost, and the user said so first.

Against which: conditionality is the whole feature and the format can't express it; reproducibility (`deploy init` has no scaffold record to pin a tag from, so unpinned `latest` is the only option — the exact thing that got `manifests create` deleted); `internal/template` has no cache and re-downloads the full repo tarball per render; and idempotency needs the CLI to know the file set and hash it, which the render-to-one-newline workaround destroys outright.

### Open questions for the user

1. **Who owns the system-scoped Dapr pubsub?** This is the top question because it has a schema consequence. `Component/pubsub` is namespace-scoped and shared by every block in the system. If each component's overlay declares it, N components produce N Applications owning the same resource → ArgoCD fights itself. Options: (a) a dedicated coordinate `domains/<d>/<s>/_system/` — but `ComponentConfig.validate` **requires** at least one `images[]` entry ("there is nothing to pin otherwise"), so shared infra cannot be a `component.yaml` today without relaxing that; (b) outside `domains/`, needing an ApplicationSet change in the GitOps repo; (c) the platform plane's job, not the integration plane's (there is a `service-setup` skill for exactly this) — init just reports "you still need a pubsub named `pubsub` in namespace `prod`". My recommendation: **(c) for the first cut, (a) as the follow-up** with an explicit `images: []` allowance for shared units. But this is the user's call and it changes the shape of `Shared`.
2. **`platform`: per-repo, per-environment, or both?** And is bumping `minimumCliVersion` in the same commit acceptable, given that older binaries hard-fail on the unknown key via `KnownFields(true)`?
3. **Where does `domain` come from long-term?** A flag every time, a new `deploy.yaml` `defaultDomain`, or recorded in the component repo's scaffold record? The topology genuinely doesn't know.
4. **Does the topology gain `schedule`?** Without it, every extractor's cron is a placeholder forever — which is *fine*, but the declaration already has the value.
5. **Branch-and-PR, or `--out <dir>`?** I've argued for branch-and-PR as the default (it contains the `ResetHard` hazard and it stops half-finished overlays reaching ArgoCD). Is a PR per onboarding acceptable in the customer's workflow, or should `--out` into their own clone be primary?
6. **Is there already a shared base in the GitOps repo?** If the platform has, say, `bases/dotnet-loader/`, then a generated overlay is `resources: [../../../../../bases/dotnet-loader]` plus a patch — and init's job shrinks from "emit a Deployment" to "emit a five-line kustomization plus Dapr components". That would make this whole plan roughly half the size, and it would make the template question nearly moot. **Worth answering before step 2.**
7. **Namespace per environment, per system, or per customer?** Drives `EnvironmentConfig.Namespace`'s default and whether Dapr component name collisions are even possible.

### Risks

- **`kustomize create` formatting drift across kustomize versions** changes hashes for files nobody edited. Mitigated by `cli:` in the record and the `--update` path; not eliminated.
- **Emitter changes are a compatibility surface.** Once a customer's GitOps repo has an `.intropy-generated.yaml`, every body template change makes files look `modified`. The record's `cli:` field makes the message honest, but this argues for treating `bodies/` as a versioned interface and being conservative with churn.
- **The `dotnet` dependency on the default path** is heavy: `dotnet build` then `dotnet run`, with a 5-minute timeout. `--topology -` must be a first-class path, documented in the Long text, so CI never needs a .NET SDK.
- **A `file`-transport connector maps to a cluster volume nobody provisioned.** Init should emit the binding with a comment saying so rather than emitting something that looks complete.
- **`--force` in a shared cached checkout** is the one genuinely dangerous mode. It's safe only because everything lands on a branch; if `--no-push` is combined with `--force`, the clobbered content lives only in a local commit on a branch that init then deletes. **Refuse `--force --no-push`** unless the branch is kept.

---

### Critical Files for Implementation

- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/gitops/config.go` — the `platform`/`namespace` schema addition, `Platform(env)`, and the `KnownFields(true)`/`minimumCliVersion` compatibility consequence
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/gitops/layout.go` — `Coordinate`, `RelPath`/`OverlayRelPath`/`AppName`, and the `notFoundError` message this command exists to make obsolete
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/deploy/plan.go` — the `assertPinsRendered` guard whose sibling `assertNoPlaceholders` becomes the gate that stops placeholders reaching the cluster
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/deploy/publish.go` — the commit/trailer format to extend, and the push machinery init deliberately does *not* reuse
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/system/codegen.go` — the in-repo precedent for the model→emitters split (and the `.WithSchedule` cron the topology doesn't yet carry)
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/topology/topology.go` — the input schema; everything the generator can and cannot know
- `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/kustomize/editor.go` — the "kustomize owns writes" rule that dictates how kustomizations get authored

content.text: Both designs converge on the same core, and the template-driven shape matches what you asked for. Four forks materially change the plan — let me settle them.

questions.question: Where should "which platform are we deploying onto" (azure vs beebyte) be declared?

options.label: deploy.yaml, repo-level (Recommended)
options.description: New optional `platform: {provider, pubsub, secretStore}` block in the GitOps repo's deploy.yaml. One customer repo = one platform. Simplest; the CLI never hardcodes "azure" — it flows deploy.yaml → template param → conditional.
options.preview:
